questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Average Value of a Function Over a Given Interval
questions.problem: During the winter in Pasadena, the temperature, in ${F}^{∘}$, $t$ hours after $9$ a.m. can be modeled by the function $T(t)=50+14\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi t}{12}).$ Find the average temperature during the period from $9$ a.m. to $9$ p.m.
questions.worked_solution:
Since the function is valid starting from $9$ A.M., we can conclude our interval is $[0,12].$

Applying the average value formula, we find that the average value of the function is

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{12-0}{\int }_{0}^{12}(50+14\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi t}{12}))\text{d}t \\  & ={\frac{1}{12}(50t-\frac{168}{\pi }\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi t}{12}))|}_{0}^{12} \\  & =\frac{1}{12}[(50\cdot 12-\frac{168}{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi \cdot 12}{12}))-(50\cdot 0-\frac{168}{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi \cdot 0}{12}))] \\  & =\frac{1}{12}[(600-\frac{168}{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi ))-(0-\frac{168}{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡(0))] \\  & =\frac{1}{12}[(600-\frac{168}{\pi }\cdot (-1))-(-\frac{168}{\pi }\cdot 1)] \\  & =\frac{1}{12}[\frac{600\pi +168}{\pi }+\frac{168}{\pi }] \\  & =\frac{1}{12}(\frac{600\pi +336}{\pi }) \\  & =\frac{600\pi +336}{12\pi } \\  & ≈{58.9}^{∘}F.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding an Interval Given the Average Value of a Function
questions.problem: Find the number $c>0$ such that the average value of $f(x)=9+8x-3{x}^{2}$ on the interval $[0,c]$ is equal to $-3.$
questions.worked_solution:
To solve for $c,$ we apply the average value formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}\,{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ -3 & =\frac{1}{c-0}\,{\int }_{0}^{c}(9+8x-3{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x \\ -3 & =\frac{1}{c}(9x+4{x}^{2}-{x}^{3}){|}_{0}^{c} \\ -3 & =\frac{1}{c}[(9c+4{c}^{2}-{c}^{3})-(0)] \\ -3 & =9+4c-{c}^{2} \\ {c}^{2}-4c-12 & =0 \\ (c+2)(c-6) & =0 \\ c & =-2,\,6\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $c>0,$ we conclude that $c=6$ only.

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Average Value of a Function Given a Graph
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14031367/assets/1c69b5a43e445861a728fcd8faed9e89b3bcb61141ad35d99e60f2a43983244d.png)

The graph of the function $f(x),$ which is defined on $[-2,9],$ is shown above. It consists of three line segments and the arc of the semi-circle centered at $(5,0)$ with radius $3.$ 

Find the average value ${f}_{\text{avg}}$ of $f(x)$ on $[0,8].$ Do not round the answer.

${f}_{\text{avg}}=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
The average value of a function on a given interval $[a,b]$ is 

$$
{f}_{\text{avg}}=\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Using the additive property of the definite integral, we write

$$
{\int }_{0}^{8}f(x)\,\text{d}x={{{\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{-{A}_{1}}+{{{\int }_{2}^{8}f(x)\,\text{d}x}_{⏟}}_{{A}_{2}}.
$$

The 1st integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [0,2].$ The corresponding region is a right triangle, so we find the area using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{1} & =\frac{1}{2}bh \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the region lies below the $x$-axis, we have 

$$
{\int }_{0}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{A}_{1}=-2.
$$

The 2nd integral represents the signed area between the curve and the $x$-axis, where $x\in [2,8].$ The corresponding region is a semi-circle, so we find the area using the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\pi {r}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\pi \cdot {3}^{2} \\  & =\frac{9\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{8}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-{A}_{1}+{A}_{2} \\  & =-2+\frac{9\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the formula for the average value, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{8-0}\cdot (-2+\frac{9\pi }{2}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}+\frac{9\pi }{16} \\  & =\frac{-4+9\pi }{16} \\  & =\frac{9\pi -4}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{(\frac{\pi }{3}-0)}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi /3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{3}{\pi }(-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)}{3})|}_{0}^{\pi /3} \\  & =\frac{3}{\pi }[(-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi ))-(-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(0))] \\  & =\frac{3}{\pi }[(-\frac{1}{3}\cdot (-1))-(-\frac{1}{3}\cdot 1)] \\  & =\frac{3}{\pi }(\frac{1}{3}+\frac{1}{3}) \\  & =\frac{3}{\pi }\cdot \frac{2}{3} \\  & =\frac{2}{\pi }.\end{aligned}
